title: No rate limiting or duplicate submission prevention on chat form
reasoning: The form checks `loading` to prevent duplicate submissions while a request is in flight, which is good. However, if the user rapidly submits multiple messages before the first completes (e.g. by clicking Send multiple times in quick succession before `loading` is set), multiple requests could be queued. Additionally, there is no client-side rate limiting to prevent abuse (e.g. spamming the API with hundreds of requests). While the `loading` guard helps, it only applies after `setLoading(true)` is called, which happens after `setMessages` and `setInput('')`. A fast double-click could theoretically send the same message twice.
reproduction:
1. Type a message
2. Rapidly double-click the Send button before the first request completes
3. Observe if two identical messages are sent (timing-dependent)
recommendation: Disable the submit button immediately on click (before async work) or use a ref-based guard to ensure only one request is in flight. Consider adding client-side rate limiting (e.g. max 5 messages per 10 seconds) to prevent abuse.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are provided. A test that simulates rapid double-click would catch this race condition.
suggestedRegressionTest: Simulate rapid form submission and verify only one request is sent. Add a test for rate limiting if implemented.
